proof:
Conventions. ℝ^P = Eucl P, ℝⁿ = Eucl n; Hᵏ := μHE[k] (Mathlib's Euclidean Hausdorff measure, equal to Lebesgue measure Lᵏ = volume on ℝᵏ); |·| is the Euclidean norm and ⟨·,·⟩ the inner product; Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x (the Fréchet derivative where it exists and 0 otherwise). Source: parent proof, Step 9 (weak-* convergence of the gradients of u_σ = h_σ∘Φ, by integration by parts against C¹ fields, density in L¹ and the uniform bound), for general uniformly convergent, uniformly Lipschitz u_k. Lⁿ = volume. e_1, …, e_n is the standard basis (EuclideanSpace.single i 1); for a vector field b we write b_i := ⟨b, e_i⟩, so b = Σ_i b_i e_i. In steps 1–4, f denotes any of the functions u, u_0, u_1, ….
1. (Pointwise bound.) For w ∈ Ω the open set Ω is a neighbourhood of w on which f is C-Lipschitz, so ‖Df(w)‖ ≤ C (`norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitzOn`; if f is not differentiable at w then Df(w) = 0).
2. (Measurability, integrability, stability.) w ↦ Df(w) is Borel measurable for every f (`measurable_fderiv`), c is Lⁿ⌞Ω-a.e. strongly measurable, and evaluation (A, s) ↦ A(s) is continuous; hence w ↦ Df(w)(c(w)) is Lⁿ⌞Ω-a.e. strongly measurable, and by step 1 it is dominated on Ω by C|c|, so it is integrable on Ω. Likewise for every field b integrable on Ω, and |∫_Ω Df(b) − ∫_Ω Df(b')| ≤ C∫_Ω|b − b'| for any two such fields b, b'.
3. (Global extension.) By McShane's extension theorem (Simon Ch. 2, 1.2; `LipschitzOnWith.extend_real`) there is f̃ : ℝⁿ → ℝ which is C-Lipschitz on ℝⁿ with f̃ = f on Ω. For w ∈ Ω the functions f and f̃ agree on the neighbourhood Ω of w, hence Df̃(w) = Df(w) (`Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq`).
4. (Integration by parts against smooth fields.) Let b : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ be C^∞ with compact support and tsupport b ⊆ Ω. Each b_i is C^∞ with compact support, hence Lipschitz on ℝⁿ (bounded derivative, mean value inequality). Put ∂_ib_i(w) := Db_i(w)e_i and div b := Σ_i ∂_ib_i, a continuous function with tsupport ⊆ tsupport b ⊆ Ω. Claim: ∫_Ω Df(w)(b(w)) dw = −∫_Ω f(w)·div b(w) dw. Indeed, b and div b vanish outside tsupport b ⊆ Ω, and on Ω f = f̃ and Df = Df̃ (step 3); so both sides equal the corresponding integrals over ℝⁿ with f̃ in place of f. By Rademacher's theorem (`LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt`) f̃ is differentiable at Lⁿ-a.e. w, and there lineDeriv ℝ f̃ w e_i = Df̃(w)e_i (`DifferentiableAt.lineDeriv_eq_fderiv`); therefore ∫ Df̃(w)(b(w)) dw = Σ_i ∫ (lineDeriv ℝ f̃ w e_i)·b_i(w) dw, where each summand is integrable: w ↦ lineDeriv ℝ f̃ w e_i is a.e. strongly measurable and essentially bounded by C (`LipschitzWith.memLp_lineDeriv` with p = ∞), and b_i is continuous with compact support. Integration by parts for Lipschitz functions (Mathlib `LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq`, Lⁿ being an additive Haar measure, b_i Lipschitz with compact support) gives ∫ (lineDeriv ℝ f̃ w e_i)·b_i(w) dw = ∫ (lineDeriv ℝ b_i w (−e_i))·f̃(w) dw = −∫ ∂_ib_i(w)·f̃(w) dw, because b_i is differentiable and lineDeriv ℝ b_i w (−e_i) = Db_i(w)(−e_i). Summing over i yields ∫Df̃(b) = −∫ f̃·div b, which is the claim.
5. (Convergence against smooth fields.) For b as in step 4, by step 4 applied to u_k and to u, |∫_Ω Du_k(b) − ∫_Ω Du(b)| = |∫_Ω (u_k − u)·div b| ≤ (sup_{w∈Ω}|u_k(w) − u(w)|)·∫|div b| → 0, since div b is continuous with compact support (so ∫|div b| < ∞) and u_k → u uniformly on Ω.
6. (Density.) For every δ > 0 there is b as in step 4 with ∫_Ω |c − b| dw < δ. Proof: Ω is σ-compact, Ω = ⋃_j K_j with K_j compact and increasing (e.g. K_j := {w ∈ Ω : |w| ≤ j, dist(w, ℝⁿ ∖ Ω) ≥ 1/j}, or closed balls if Ω = ℝⁿ); by dominated convergence ∫_{Ω∖K_j}|c| → 0, so fix j with ∫_{Ω∖K_j}|c| < δ/2. The field 1_{K_j}c is Lⁿ-integrable on ℝⁿ, so there is a C^∞ compactly supported b₀ with ∫|1_{K_j}c − b₀| < δ/2 (density of C_c^∞ in L¹, Mathlib `MeasureTheory.MemLp.exist_eLpNorm_sub_le` with p = 1, import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Lp.SmoothApprox). Choose an open W with K_j ⊆ W, closure W compact and contained in Ω, and a C^∞ function χ : ℝⁿ → [0, 1] with support χ = W and χ = 1 exactly on K_j (smooth Urysohn lemma, Mathlib `exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff`). Put b := χ·b₀: it is C^∞ with compact support and tsupport b ⊆ closure W ⊆ Ω. As χ1_{K_j} = 1_{K_j} and 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, 1_{K_j}c − b = χ(1_{K_j}c − b₀), so ∫|1_{K_j}c − b| ≤ ∫|1_{K_j}c − b₀| < δ/2. Hence ∫_Ω|c − b| ≤ ∫_{Ω∖K_j}|c| + ∫|1_{K_j}c − b| < δ.
7. (Conclusion.) Let ε > 0, δ := ε/(3(C + 1)), and choose b by step 6. By step 2, for every k, |∫_Ω Du_k(c) − ∫_Ω Du_k(b)| ≤ Cδ < ε/3 and |∫_Ω Du(b) − ∫_Ω Du(c)| < ε/3. By step 5 there is k₀ with |∫_Ω Du_k(b) − ∫_Ω Du(b)| < ε/3 for k ≥ k₀. Hence |∫_Ω Du_k(c) − ∫_Ω Du(c)| < ε for k ≥ k₀. ∎
key_steps: ‖Df‖ ≤ C on Ω for f ∈ {u, u_k}; the integrands are measurable and dominated by C|c|.
Integration by parts on Ω for C-Lipschitz f and C^∞ fields b with compact support in Ω: ∫_Ω Df(b) = −∫_Ω f div b (McShane extension, Rademacher, LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq).
Uniform convergence on Ω gives ∫_Ω Du_k(b) → ∫_Ω Du(b) for such b.
C^∞ fields with compact support in Ω are dense in L¹(Ω; ℝⁿ); an ε/3 argument with the uniform bound C finishes.
